title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is a mixed bag of resilience and challenges, with NASA and ESA dodging wildfires while ULA grapples with financial woes. Meanwhile, SpaceX continues its relentless pursuit of Starship testing, and the defense sector sees a surge in AI interest.

themes.title: Wildfires and Resilience
themes.body: NASA and ESA facilities in Spain have emerged largely unscathed from recent wildfires, showcasing the sector's ability to weather environmental challenges. This incident underscores the importance of infrastructure resilience in the face of increasing climate-related threats.

themes.title: Starship's Ongoing Trials
themes.body: SpaceX's 13th Starship test flight indicates a relentless push towards operational readiness, despite the setbacks that have characterized previous attempts. Each flight brings the company closer to its ambitious goals, but the road remains bumpy.

themes.title: Financial Strains at ULA
themes.body: United Launch Alliance is feeling the financial pinch as the Vulcan rocket remains grounded, raising questions about its future viability. This situation highlights the precarious balance between innovation and fiscal responsibility in the aerospace sector.

themes.title: AI's Defense Surge
themes.body: The growing interest in AI capabilities for defense, as evidenced by LatConnect 60's new offerings, reflects a broader trend of technological integration in military operations. This shift could redefine operational strategies as defense contractors scramble to keep pace.
